subject: Reserved commit tiers, onboarding timeline & phased capacity start
messages:
From: Hugo Ramirez <hugo@altitudehealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved capacity — timing / discount question

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput and latency numbers look promising. Procurement asked me to follow up on two things before we bring this to budget: 1) we need clarity on the minimum commit term you’re willing to lock for the discounted pricing (our finance prefers 12 or 24 months, not 36), and 2) the earliest practical start date if we sign this month.

Also, given our seasonal traffic spike in Q4, we’d like a phased onramp rather than an all-in start. Can you outline a simple option set (12/24/36) with corresponding discounts and an example phased ramp schedule tied to billing?

Appreciate a concise table we can take to shows/finance.

—Hugo
Head of ML Ops
Altitude Health
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Hugo Ramirez <hugo@altitudehealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved capacity — timing / discount question

Hugo — appreciate the clear asks. High level options below; attaching a short term sheet and a sample phased-capacity plan.

Summary (all prices in USD / monthly invoice):
- 12-month commit: baseline pool (8 GPUs equiv) — 12% discount off list, onboarding credit: 2 weeks free; start date within 30 days of signature.
- 24-month commit: baseline pool (10 GPUs equiv) — 18% discount, onboarding credit: 1 month free; start date within 21 days.
- 36-month commit: baseline pool (12 GPUs equiv) — 25% discount, onboarding credit: 6 weeks free; start date within 14 days.

Phased onramp example (flexible):
- Month 1: 50% capacity (warm-up)
- Month 3: 80% capacity
- Month 6: 100% capacity (full pool)

Throughput guarantees / SLOs: committed RPS target per pool with 99th percentile latency bands. If we miss target >2 consecutive days, automated credit backstop kicks in (details in term sheet).

Next steps: if 12- or 24-month is preferred I can produce a versioned term sheet with exact monthly numbers and a DocuSign link. Marcus/aditya — can you confirm GPU-equivalent assumptions (A100 vs H100 mix) and a rough monthly token throughput for the sample above?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Attachment: Altitude_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf; capacity_plan_altitude.xlsx
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Hugo Ramirez <hugo@altitudehealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved capacity — sizing & throughput note

Hugo, Lauren — quick technical sizing note to align expectations.

Assumptions we used for the term sheet:
- Baseline model mix: 60% chat/interactive gen (avg len 80 tokens), 40% embedding/rerank.
- Equivalent GPUs: we recommended A100-80GB parity for pricing. 1x A100 equiv sustained will give ~180 prompt+generate tokens/sec for the chat mix above (subject to prompt length).
- 8 GPU pool -> rough steady-state throughput: ~1.4M tokens/min (burst to 2.2M tokens/min with autoscaling buffer).

If Altitude expects heavier batched embedding workloads, swap 2 of the baseline GPUs for higher-memory H100 class; that increases batched embedding throughput ~30% but reduces single-request latency slightly.

I’ll add a column in the capacity_plan_altitude.xlsx for the different mix scenarios so procurement can see cost/perf tradeoffs.

- Aditya (SE)
From: Hugo Ramirez <hugo@altitudehealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Altitude Health Procurement <procurement@altitudehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved capacity — sizing & throughput note

Thanks — that helps. A few follow-ups: 1) Our finance team is adamant that 36 months is a hard no; they want a 12-month base with an option to extend at the same pricing for another 12 months. Would you consider a 12+12 rollover at the 24-month discount tier (i.e., price locked if we exercise extension within a 60 day window)? 2) Can you carve out a ramp credit if we stick to the phased onramp (e.g., if we stay below 70% for first 2 months, apply partial invoice credit)? 3) Contract start: our legal wants to see a clear definition of 'capacity start' vs 'billing start' — ideally billing only starts when the pool is at 50% warmed.

If you can accept (1) and (2) and clarify (3) we can route to legal next week.

—Hugo
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Hugo Ramirez <hugo@altitudehealth.com>, procurement@altitudehealth.com
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved capacity — sizing & throughput note

Hugo — we can be flexible on the points you raised. Proposed concessions: 1) 12+12 rollover: we’ll offer a 12-month initial term with an automatic right for Altitude to extend for a second 12 months at the 24-month discount rate, provided the extension is exercised within a 60-day window before term end. Extension will require mutual confirmation but price will be locked.
2) Ramp credit: yes — if average utilization <70% for first 60 days we apply a pro-rated onboarding credit applied to invoices for month 2 and 3 (specific formula in the attached term sheet).
3) Capacity vs billing start: we define \"capacity start\" as the date the reserved GPU pool is provisioned and reachable by Altitude; \"billing start\" will be the first UTC day when provisioned capacity reaches >=50% of contracted baseline for a sustained 48-hour window. If we fail to reach 50% within 30 days, option to pause billing or mutually agree to a new timeline.

I’ve asked Rachel (legal) to review and will push a redline with those clauses included. If that looks good we’ll generate a DocuSign for signature.

Best,
Lauren
Attachment: Altitude_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (updated with rollover + ramp credit language)
From: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Reserved commit — redline and next steps

Hugo / Altitude legal — attaching a redlined contract with the 12+12 rollover language, ramp-credit formula, and the billing vs capacity start definition we discussed. A couple of notes from my side:
- We included a hard cap on the onboarding credit equal to one full monthly invoice; any adjustments beyond that will be handled via a separate commercial amendment.
- We added a short SLA appendix that defines throughput measurement methodology (token-based telemetry) and the credit trigger threshold.

Attachments: redline_Altitude_Dedicated_Commit.docx
